  "claims": [
    {"id":"f1","concept_id":"c1","text":"A checkpoint moves WAL transactions back into the database.","source_id":"S1","quote":"Moving the WAL file transactions back into the database is called a \" checkpoint \".","pass":0},
    {"id":"f2","concept_id":"c2","text":"The default automatic checkpoint threshold is 1000 WAL pages.","source_id":"S1","quote":"By default, SQLite does a checkpoint automatically when the WAL file reaches a threshold size of 1000 pages.","pass":0},
    {"id":"f3","concept_id":"c6","text":"Automatically initiated checkpoints use PASSIVE mode.","source_id":"S1","quote":"All checkpoints initiated by sqlite3_wal_checkpoint() and by the automatic checkpoint mechanism are PASSIVE.","pass":0},
    {"id":"f4","concept_id":"c3","text":"A checkpoint must stop at a WAL page past any current reader's end mark.","source_id":"S1","quote":"A checkpoint can run concurrently with readers, however the checkpoint must stop when it reaches a page in the WAL that is past the end mark of any current reader.","pass":0},
    {"id":"f5","concept_id":"c3","text":"A checkpoint records progress in the wal-index so the next invocation resumes where it stopped.","source_id":"S1","quote":"The checkpoint remembers (in the wal-index) how far it got and will resume transferring content from the WAL to the database from where it left off on the next invocation.","pass":0},
    {"id":"f6","concept_id":"c4","text":"The WAL must be synced to persistent storage before checkpoint content is moved into the database.","source_id":"S1","quote":"The WAL must be synced to persistent storage prior to moving content from the WAL into the database","pass":0},
    {"id":"f7","concept_id":"c4","text":"The database file must be synced before the WAL is reset.","source_id":"S1","quote":"and the database file must be synced prior to resetting the WAL.","pass":0},
    {"id":"f8","concept_id":"c5","text":"Checkpointing normally does not truncate the WAL file, with journal_size_limit identified as an exception.","source_id":"S1","quote":"The checkpoint does not normally truncate the WAL file (unless the journal_size_limit pragma is set).","pass":0},

    {"id":"f9","concept_id":"c7","text":"SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_FULL invokes the busy handler while waiting for no writer and for all readers to use the most recent database snapshot.","source_id":"S2","quote":"SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_FULL This mode blocks (it invokes the busy-handler callback ) until there is no database writer and all readers are reading from the most recent database snapshot.","pass":1},
    {"id":"f10","concept_id":"c7","text":"A pending SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_FULL blocks new writers while allowing new readers to proceed.","source_id":"S2","quote":"This mode blocks new database writers while it is pending, but new database readers are allowed to continue unimpeded.","pass":1},
    {"id":"f11","concept_id":"c8","text":"SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_RESTART adds a post-checkpoint wait until all readers read only from the database file.","source_id":"S2","quote":"This mode works the same way as SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_FULL with the addition that after checkpointing the log file it blocks (calls the busy-handler callback ) until all readers are reading from the database file only.","pass":1},
    {"id":"f12","concept_id":"c8","text":"SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_RESTART's additional reader wait ensures the next writer restarts the WAL from the beginning.","source_id":"S2","quote":"This ensures that the next writer will restart the log file from the beginning.","pass":1},
    {"id":"f13","concept_id":"c9","text":"SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_TRUNCATE adds truncation to zero bytes immediately before a successful return to RESTART behavior.","source_id":"S2","quote":"SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_TRUNCATE This mode works the same way as SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_RESTART with the addition that it also truncates the log file to zero bytes just prior to a successful return.","pass":1},
    {"id":"f14","concept_id":"c10","text":"SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_NOOP checkpoints zero frames and exists to retrieve checkpoint output counters.","source_id":"S2","quote":"SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_NOOP This mode always checkpoints zero frames. The only reason to invoke a NOOP checkpoint is to access the values returned by sqlite3_wal_checkpoint_v2() via output parameters *pnLog and *pnCkpt.","pass":1},
    {"id":"f15","concept_id":"c6","text":"SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_PASSIVE never invokes the busy-handler callback.","source_id":"S2","quote":"The busy-handler callback is never invoked in the SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_PASSIVE mode. On the other hand, passive mode might leave the checkpoint unfinished","pass":1},
    {"id":"f16","concept_id":"c6","text":"SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_PASSIVE syncs the database file if it checkpoints all frames in the log.","source_id":"S2","quote":"Checkpoint as many frames as possible without waiting for any database readers or writers to finish, then sync the database file if all frames in the log were checkpointed.","pass":1},
    {"id":"f17","concept_id":"c3","text":"The reader end-mark stopping rule prevents checkpointing from overwriting database content a reader is actively using.","source_id":"S1","quote":"The checkpoint has to stop at that point because otherwise it might overwrite part of the database file that the reader is actively using.","pass":1},
    {"id":"f18","concept_id":"c13","text":"Continuously overlapping active readers can prevent checkpoint completion and cause unbounded WAL growth.","source_id":"S1","quote":"However, if a database has many concurrent overlapping readers and there is always at least one active reader, then no checkpoints will be able to complete and hence the WAL file will grow without bound.","pass":1},

    {"id":"f19","concept_id":"c11","text":"Concurrent checkpoint activity can prevent acquisition of the exclusive checkpoint lock and return SQLITE_BUSY.","source_id":"S2","quote":"All calls obtain an exclusive \"checkpoint\" lock on the database file. If any other process is running a checkpoint operation at the same time, the lock cannot be obtained and SQLITE_BUSY is returned.","pass":2},
    {"id":"f20","concept_id":"c11","text":"Checkpoint-lock contention does not invoke the busy handler even when one is configured.","source_id":"S2","quote":"Even if there is a busy-handler configured, it will not be invoked in this case.","pass":2},
    {"id":"f21","concept_id":"c11","text":"SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_FULL, SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_RESTART, and SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_TRUNCATE also acquire the exclusive writer lock.","source_id":"S2","quote":"The SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_FULL, RESTART and TRUNCATE modes also obtain the exclusive \"writer\" lock on the database file.","pass":2},
    {"id":"f22","concept_id":"c11","text":"If the busy handler returns zero before writer-lock acquisition or while waiting for readers, checkpointing falls back to SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_PASSIVE behavior.","source_id":"S2","quote":"If the busy-handler returns 0 before the writer lock is obtained or while waiting for database readers, the checkpoint operation proceeds from that point in the same way as SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_PASSIVE","pass":2},
    {"id":"f23","concept_id":"c2","text":"Passing N less than or equal to zero to sqlite3_wal_autocheckpoint disables automatic checkpoints entirely.","source_id":"S3","quote":"Passing zero or a negative value as the N parameter disables automatic checkpoints entirely.","pass":2},
    {"id":"f24","concept_id":"c2","text":"sqlite3_wal_autocheckpoint replaces any callback previously registered using sqlite3_wal_hook.","source_id":"S3","quote":"The callback registered by this function replaces any existing callback registered using sqlite3_wal_hook() .","pass":2},
    {"id":"f25","concept_id":"c2","text":"Registering a callback using sqlite3_wal_hook disables automatic checkpointing configured by sqlite3_wal_autocheckpoint.","source_id":"S3","quote":"Likewise, registering a callback using sqlite3_wal_hook() disables the automatic checkpoint mechanism configured by this function.","pass":2},
    {"id":"f26","concept_id":"c12","text":"The pnCkpt output includes frames checkpointed before the current call.","source_id":"S2","quote":"*pnCkpt is set to the total number of checkpointed frames in the log file (including any that were already checkpointed before the function was called)","pass":2},
    {"id":"f27","concept_id":"c12","text":"Successful SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_TRUNCATE sets both pnLog and pnCkpt outputs to zero.","source_id":"S2","quote":"Note that upon successful completion of an SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_TRUNCATE, the log file will have been truncated to zero bytes and so both *pnLog and *pnCkpt will be set to zero.","pass":2},
    {"id":"f28","concept_id":"c13","text":"Attempting checkpoints during reader gaps can avoid starvation caused by continuously overlapping readers.","source_id":"S1","quote":"This scenario can be avoided by ensuring that there are \"reader gaps\": times when no processes are reading from the database and that checkpoints are attempted during those times.","pass":2},

    {"id":"f29","concept_id":"c12","text":"For a named attached database outside WAL mode, the checkpoint API returns SQLITE_OK and sets both counters to -1.","source_id":"S2","quote":"If database zDb is the name of an attached database that is not in WAL mode, SQLITE_OK is returned and both *pnLog and *pnCkpt set to -1.","pass":3},
    {"id":"f30","concept_id":"c12","text":"A checkpoint operation targeting all attached WAL databases has undefined pnLog and pnCkpt outputs.","source_id":"S2","quote":"then the specified operation is attempted on all WAL databases attached to database connection db. In this case the values written to output parameters *pnLog and *pnCkpt are undefined.","pass":3},
    {"id":"f31","concept_id":"c12","text":"During an operation across attached WAL databases, SQLITE_BUSY does not prevent attempts on remaining databases and is returned at the end.","source_id":"S2","quote":"If an SQLITE_BUSY error is encountered when processing one or more of the attached WAL databases, the operation is still attempted on any remaining attached databases and SQLITE_BUSY is returned at the end.","pass":3},
    {"id":"f32","concept_id":"c12","text":"During an operation across attached databases, an error other than SQLITE_BUSY abandons processing and returns immediately.","source_id":"S2","quote":"If any other error occurs while processing an attached database, processing is abandoned and the error code is returned to the caller immediately.","pass":3},
    {"id":"f33","concept_id":"c15","text":"As of SQLite 3.11.0, dated 2016-02-15, a single transaction's WAL file should be proportional in size to the transaction.","source_id":"S1","quote":"As of SQLite version 3.11.0 (2016-02-15), the WAL file for a single transaction should be proportional in size to the transaction itself.","pass":3},
    {"id":"f34","concept_id":"c15","text":"Older SQLite versions could write the same page into the WAL multiple times when a transaction exceeded the page cache.","source_id":"S1","quote":"However, with older versions of SQLite, the same page might be written into the WAL file multiple times if the transaction grows larger than the page cache.","pass":3},
    {"id":"f35","concept_id":"c14","text":"COMMIT operations that trigger checkpoints can be much slower than other COMMIT operations.","source_id":"S1","quote":"This has the effect of causing most COMMIT operations to be very fast but an occasional COMMIT (those that trigger a checkpoint) to be much slower.","pass":3},
    {"id":"f36","concept_id":"c4","text":"With PRAGMA synchronous set to NORMAL, checkpointing is the only operation that issues an I/O barrier or sync operation.","source_id":"S1","quote":"Note that with PRAGMA synchronous set to NORMAL, the checkpoint is the only operation to issue an I/O barrier or sync operation (fsync() on unix or FlushFileBuffers() on windows).","pass":3}

claims.text: A checkpoint moves WAL transactions back into the database.
claims.quote: Moving the WAL file transactions back into the database is called a " checkpoint ".

claims.text: The default automatic checkpoint threshold is 1000 WAL pages.
claims.quote: By default, SQLite does a checkpoint automatically when the WAL file reaches a threshold size of 1000 pages.

claims.text: Automatically initiated checkpoints use PASSIVE mode.
claims.quote: All checkpoints initiated by sqlite3_wal_checkpoint() and by the automatic checkpoint mechanism are PASSIVE.

claims.text: A checkpoint must stop at a WAL page past any current reader's end mark.
claims.quote: A checkpoint can run concurrently with readers, however the checkpoint must stop when it reaches a page in the WAL that is past the end mark of any current reader.

claims.text: A checkpoint records progress in the wal-index so the next invocation resumes where it stopped.
claims.quote: The checkpoint remembers (in the wal-index) how far it got and will resume transferring content from the WAL to the database from where it left off on the next invocation.

claims.text: The WAL must be synced to persistent storage before checkpoint content is moved into the database.
claims.quote: The WAL must be synced to persistent storage prior to moving content from the WAL into the database

claims.text: The database file must be synced before the WAL is reset.
claims.quote: and the database file must be synced prior to resetting the WAL.

claims.text: Checkpointing normally does not truncate the WAL file, with journal_size_limit identified as an exception.
claims.quote: The checkpoint does not normally truncate the WAL file (unless the journal_size_limit pragma is set).

claims.text: SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_FULL invokes the busy handler while waiting for no writer and for all readers to use the most recent database snapshot.
claims.quote: SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_FULL This mode blocks (it invokes the busy-handler callback ) until there is no database writer and all readers are reading from the most recent database snapshot.

claims.text: A pending SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_FULL blocks new writers while allowing new readers to proceed.
claims.quote: This mode blocks new database writers while it is pending, but new database readers are allowed to continue unimpeded.

claims.text: SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_RESTART adds a post-checkpoint wait until all readers read only from the database file.
claims.quote: This mode works the same way as SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_FULL with the addition that after checkpointing the log file it blocks (calls the busy-handler callback ) until all readers are reading from the database file only.

claims.text: SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_RESTART's additional reader wait ensures the next writer restarts the WAL from the beginning.
claims.quote: This ensures that the next writer will restart the log file from the beginning.

claims.text: SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_TRUNCATE adds truncation to zero bytes immediately before a successful return to RESTART behavior.
claims.quote: SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_TRUNCATE This mode works the same way as SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_RESTART with the addition that it also truncates the log file to zero bytes just prior to a successful return.

claims.text: SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_NOOP checkpoints zero frames and exists to retrieve checkpoint output counters.
claims.quote: SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_NOOP This mode always checkpoints zero frames. The only reason to invoke a NOOP checkpoint is to access the values returned by sqlite3_wal_checkpoint_v2() via output parameters *pnLog and *pnCkpt.

claims.text: SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_PASSIVE never invokes the busy-handler callback.
claims.quote: The busy-handler callback is never invoked in the SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_PASSIVE mode. On the other hand, passive mode might leave the checkpoint unfinished

claims.text: SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_PASSIVE syncs the database file if it checkpoints all frames in the log.
claims.quote: Checkpoint as many frames as possible without waiting for any database readers or writers to finish, then sync the database file if all frames in the log were checkpointed.

claims.text: The reader end-mark stopping rule prevents checkpointing from overwriting database content a reader is actively using.
claims.quote: The checkpoint has to stop at that point because otherwise it might overwrite part of the database file that the reader is actively using.

claims.text: Continuously overlapping active readers can prevent checkpoint completion and cause unbounded WAL growth.
claims.quote: However, if a database has many concurrent overlapping readers and there is always at least one active reader, then no checkpoints will be able to complete and hence the WAL file will grow without bound.

claims.text: Concurrent checkpoint activity can prevent acquisition of the exclusive checkpoint lock and return SQLITE_BUSY.
claims.quote: All calls obtain an exclusive "checkpoint" lock on the database file. If any other process is running a checkpoint operation at the same time, the lock cannot be obtained and SQLITE_BUSY is returned.

claims.text: Checkpoint-lock contention does not invoke the busy handler even when one is configured.
claims.quote: Even if there is a busy-handler configured, it will not be invoked in this case.

claims.text: SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_FULL, SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_RESTART, and SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_TRUNCATE also acquire the exclusive writer lock.
claims.quote: The SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_FULL, RESTART and TRUNCATE modes also obtain the exclusive "writer" lock on the database file.

claims.text: If the busy handler returns zero before writer-lock acquisition or while waiting for readers, checkpointing falls back to SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_PASSIVE behavior.
claims.quote: If the busy-handler returns 0 before the writer lock is obtained or while waiting for database readers, the checkpoint operation proceeds from that point in the same way as SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_PASSIVE

claims.text: Passing N less than or equal to zero to sqlite3_wal_autocheckpoint disables automatic checkpoints entirely.
claims.quote: Passing zero or a negative value as the N parameter disables automatic checkpoints entirely.

claims.text: sqlite3_wal_autocheckpoint replaces any callback previously registered using sqlite3_wal_hook.
claims.quote: The callback registered by this function replaces any existing callback registered using sqlite3_wal_hook() .

claims.text: Registering a callback using sqlite3_wal_hook disables automatic checkpointing configured by sqlite3_wal_autocheckpoint.
claims.quote: Likewise, registering a callback using sqlite3_wal_hook() disables the automatic checkpoint mechanism configured by this function.

claims.text: The pnCkpt output includes frames checkpointed before the current call.
claims.quote: *pnCkpt is set to the total number of checkpointed frames in the log file (including any that were already checkpointed before the function was called)

claims.text: Successful SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_TRUNCATE sets both pnLog and pnCkpt outputs to zero.
claims.quote: Note that upon successful completion of an SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_TRUNCATE, the log file will have been truncated to zero bytes and so both *pnLog and *pnCkpt will be set to zero.

claims.text: Attempting checkpoints during reader gaps can avoid starvation caused by continuously overlapping readers.
claims.quote: This scenario can be avoided by ensuring that there are "reader gaps": times when no processes are reading from the database and that checkpoints are attempted during those times.

claims.text: For a named attached database outside WAL mode, the checkpoint API returns SQLITE_OK and sets both counters to -1.
claims.quote: If database zDb is the name of an attached database that is not in WAL mode, SQLITE_OK is returned and both *pnLog and *pnCkpt set to -1.

claims.text: A checkpoint operation targeting all attached WAL databases has undefined pnLog and pnCkpt outputs.
claims.quote: then the specified operation is attempted on all WAL databases attached to database connection db. In this case the values written to output parameters *pnLog and *pnCkpt are undefined.

claims.text: During an operation across attached WAL databases, SQLITE_BUSY does not prevent attempts on remaining databases and is returned at the end.
claims.quote: If an SQLITE_BUSY error is encountered when processing one or more of the attached WAL databases, the operation is still attempted on any remaining attached databases and SQLITE_BUSY is returned at the end.

claims.text: During an operation across attached databases, an error other than SQLITE_BUSY abandons processing and returns immediately.
claims.quote: If any other error occurs while processing an attached database, processing is abandoned and the error code is returned to the caller immediately.

claims.text: As of SQLite 3.11.0, dated 2016-02-15, a single transaction's WAL file should be proportional in size to the transaction.
claims.quote: As of SQLite version 3.11.0 (2016-02-15), the WAL file for a single transaction should be proportional in size to the transaction itself.

claims.text: Older SQLite versions could write the same page into the WAL multiple times when a transaction exceeded the page cache.
claims.quote: However, with older versions of SQLite, the same page might be written into the WAL file multiple times if the transaction grows larger than the page cache.

claims.text: COMMIT operations that trigger checkpoints can be much slower than other COMMIT operations.
claims.quote: This has the effect of causing most COMMIT operations to be very fast but an occasional COMMIT (those that trigger a checkpoint) to be much slower.

claims.text: With PRAGMA synchronous set to NORMAL, checkpointing is the only operation that issues an I/O barrier or sync operation.
claims.quote: Note that with PRAGMA synchronous set to NORMAL, the checkpoint is the only operation to issue an I/O barrier or sync operation (fsync() on unix or FlushFileBuffers() on windows).
